summary:
Andrew Boyd’s 2017 essay *12 Characters in Search of an Apocalypse* presents twelve fictional perspectives on how people in the United States experience climate change. The essays show varied responses to the crisis, including fear, denial, hope, and action.

In August 2017, Giraffe Social Enterprises began touring a participatory version of the work in Wales and England. The events combined readings with facilitated conversations about climate change and its effects on communities. By January 2020, gatherings had also taken place in several other countries. Extinction Rebellion activists used the work to engage people with the climate crisis.

Boyd later added seven characters online. He planned to include the essays in a book, *I Want a Better Catastrophe: 69 Paradoxes for Surviving the 21st Century*.
